query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin, uniform metallic interlayer (such as via electroless nickel plating) on the tungsten surfaces prior to composite consolidation will inhibit W–Cu phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A W–Cu composite consisting of tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten ligaments embedded in a copper matrix, which otherwise exhibits phase separation and interfacial void formation when exposed to elevated temperatures and irradiation.
generation.intervention: Pre-coating the tungsten particles/ligaments with a thin nickel layer (using electroless plating) before the composite is processed (e.g., via powder metallurgy consolidation).
generation.conditions: The coated composite is fabricated using standard powder metallurgy (or similar consolidation) and subsequently subjected to thermal cycling and controlled irradiation conditions that mimic the joint environments between W-based plasma-facing surfaces and Cu-based cooling components.
generation.structural_mediator: A stable, continuous nickel interlayer at the W–Cu interfaces.
generation.mechanism: The nickel layer acts as a diffusion barrier and enhances wetting between tungsten and copper. It minimizes interdiffusion-driven phase separation and interfacial void formation by reducing the interfacial energy and stabilizing the interface under thermal and irradiation stress.
generation.predicted_outcome: The nickel-coated composite will exhibit improved thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite, owing to the preserved interfacial integrity and reduced void content.
generation.baseline: An untreated W–Cu composite that, under similar heat-transfer and irradiation conditions, develops phase separation and interfacial voids leading to degraded thermal conductivity.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected under processing conditions typical of powder metallurgy for these composites and service conditions (temperature cycling and irradiation) relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing components and Cu-based cooling systems.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the improvement in thermal conductivity and long-term durability under actual service irradiation conditions remain to be quantitatively validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Two sets of samples will be prepared: one set of W–Cu composites with tungsten particles pre-coated by electroless nickel plating, and a control set without coating. Both sets will be consolidated via identical powder metallurgy routes. Samples will then be subjected to accelerated thermal cycling (at temperatures representative of joint operating conditions) and controlled ion-beam irradiation to simulate neutron damage. Post-treatment, the samples will be analyzed using microscopy (SEM/TEM) to assess interfacial integrity and void content, and thermal conductivity will be measured using laser flash analysis.
measurements: Interfacial microstructure (SEM/TEM imaging and EDS mapping for element distribution)
Thermal conductivity via laser flash analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nickel-coated samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in interfacial integrity (i.e., reduced void formation and phase separation) and thermal conductivity compared to the untreated control, the hypothesis will be falsified.
